one_line_description.value: Otter.ai's Public API provides programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details from an Otter account.
one_line_description.quote: Otter.ai’s Public API provides programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details from your Otter account.

has_public_api.quote: Otter's Public API is available for all Enterprise workspaces.

api_breadth.value: REST v1, read/retrieval-oriented endpoints for channels, channel members, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details; Super Admin APIs add workspace-wide conversation access.
api_breadth.quote: Otter APIs provide programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details from your Otter account.

access_model.quote: Otter's Public API is available for all Enterprise workspaces. If you do not see this feature for your workspace, contact your Otter account manager.

access_notes.value: Enterprise-only: Otter's Public API is available for all Enterprise workspaces; if it is not visible for a workspace, access must be enabled by contacting your Otter account manager. The Otter MCP server is a separate OAuth-based integration that appears in AI-assistant connector directories.
access_notes.quote: Otter's Public API is available for all Enterprise workspaces. If you do not see this feature for your workspace, contact your Otter account manager.

official_mcp_server.quote: Connect AI models to Otter using Model Context Protocol (MCP).

rate_limits.value: 10 requests/second for Enterprise plan users; exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
rate_limits.quote: Enterprise plan users are currently limited to 10 requests / second. If you exceed your rate limit, you'll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response.

webhooks.quote: Webhooks are the recommended way to build export integrations with Otter.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: API paths are versioned in the URL (v1, e.g. https://api.otter.ai/v1/...); no deprecation or sunset policy is documented in the evidence.

verdict_reason: Otter documents a Public API, but it is available only for Enterprise workspaces, and access must be enabled by contacting an Otter account manager. Rate limits and webhooks are documented, but the Enterprise/account-manager gate means a third-party developer cannot self-serve credentials for the REST API. Otter separately offers an OAuth-based MCP server for AI assistants, but the documented developer REST API remains contact-sales gated.
main_blocker: Public API restricted to Enterprise workspaces and enabled via Otter account manager
outreach_reason: A third-party developer needs an Otter Enterprise workspace and must contact their Otter account manager to enable Public API access.
open_questions: OAuth scopes/permissions for the Otter MCP server are not enumerated in the evidence.
No sandbox or test environment for the Otter Public API is documented in the evidence.
No official vendor-maintained SDKs are documented in the evidence.
API deprecation/sunset policy beyond the v1 URL path is not documented.
The exact Otter MCP endpoint URL is not published; setup is described through Claude/ChatGPT connector directories.
Does the OAuth-based Otter MCP server available on consumer plans provide a self-serve alternative to the Enterprise-gated Public REST API?
No community MCP servers were found in the evidence (GitHub and MCP registry checks returned none).
